title: Composition of kernel transforms
statement:
Use the geometric finite-field and $E$-adic coefficient setting of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. The notation $D^b_c(-,E)$ means the rationalized derived-complete constructible category, with completed integral operations rationalized as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $V\to S$, $V^\vee\to S$, $V''\to S$ be separated finite-type morphisms. The superscript $\vee$ is just a name in the general assertion. Products are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

Let $\mathcal K\in D^b_c(V\times_SV^\vee,E)$, $\mathcal K'\in D^b_c(V^\vee\times_SV'',E)$, and $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. With projections $p_i,q_i$ of these two products define
$$
\Phi_{\mathcal K}(M)=Rp_{2,!}(Lp_1^*M\otimes^L_E\mathcal K)[a],\qquad
\Phi_{\mathcal K'}(N)=Rq_{2,!}(Lq_1^*N\otimes^L_E\mathcal K')[b].
$$
Then there is an isomorphism of functors, natural in $M$ and in both kernels,
$$
\Phi_{\mathcal K'}\circ\Phi_{\mathcal K}\simeq
\bigl(M\longmapsto Rs_{2,!}(Ls_1^*M\otimes^L_E(\mathcal K'\ast\mathcal K))[a+b]\bigr),
$$
where $s_1,s_2$ are the projections of $V\times_SV''$ and
$$
\mathcal K'\ast\mathcal K:=Rr_{13,!}(Lr_{12}^*\mathcal K\otimes^L_E Lr_{23}^*\mathcal K')\in D^b_c(V\times_SV'',E),
$$
with $r_{ij}$ the projections of $V\times_SV^\vee\times_SV''$.

In particular, when $V$ is a vector bundle of rank $r\ge0$, $V^\vee$ its dual, $V''$ its bidual, and $E$ contains the values of the chosen additive character $\psi$, take the two Artin--Schreier kernels $\mathcal K_\psi,\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}$ of [def-fd-kernel] for the evaluation pairings, regarded in $D^b_c(-,E)$ as the rationalizations at $E$ of their completed realizations $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{adic}}_{\Psi^{\pm1},b}$ of [def-fd-adic-fourier-realization], and $a=b=r$. For the $E$-adic Fourier transforms defined by the displayed formulas, $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is the transform with kernel $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\ast\mathcal K_\psi$ and shift $[2r]$. Here the $E$-adic convention is the one of [def-fourier-set]; it is not the derived category of discrete $E$-module sheaves on the small etale site.

proof.text: Put $T=V\times_SV^\vee\times_SV''$, $P=V\times_SV^\vee$, $Q=V^\vee\times_SV''$, and $H=V\times_SV''$. The square with top $r_{12}:T\to P$, bottom $q_1:Q\to V^\vee$, and verticals $r_{23},p_2$ is Cartesian: a map into its fibre product specifies the three maps to $V,V^\vee,V''$ with equal maps to $S$. Thus its universal property is exactly that of $T$. Every projection forgetting a factor is a base change of that factor's structure map to $S$, hence separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Successive such projections give finite-type product schemes by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]; they are separated over $k$ because the product diagonal is cut out by the closed diagonals of its factors. Set $r_1=p_1r_{12}=s_1r_{13}$ and $r_3=q_2r_{23}=s_2r_{13}$; these are identities of the corresponding projections. The constructible-domain assertion of [prop-functor-package] ensures that all pullbacks, tensors and compact-support images below, including the convolution, lie in $D^b_c(-,E)$.

First remove the two prescribed shifts. Pullback and extension by zero are termwise at finite level and commute with cochain shifts. If $I$ resolves a complex, $I[a]$ is again a K-injective resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], so proper derived direct image also commutes with shifts. These facts apply to the finite-level compactification formula for $Rf_!$ in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The completed operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] use the functorial product mapping-fiber model: product commutes with shift degreewise and the cone comparison is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^a y)$. Hence these shift comparisons pass to the integral operations and then to their rationalizations. The tensor comparison in the second slot is [lem-sf-completed-tensor-shift-right]; signed symmetry gives it in the first slot, and the same comparison rationalizes. Since $C[a][b]=C[a+b]$ with the cochain differential convention, the composite equals the unshifted composite followed by $[a+b]$. Each comparison is natural in the input and kernels.

For $M\in D^b_c(V,E)$ put $A=Lp_1^*M\otimes^L_E\mathcal K$. Substitute the definitions without the shifts. The compact-support base-change clause of [prop-functor-package], applied to the Cartesian square in step 1, gives
$$
Rq_{2,!}(Lq_1^*Rp_{2,!}A\otimes^L_E\mathcal K')\simeq Rq_{2,!}(Rr_{23,!}Lr_{12}^*A\otimes^L_E\mathcal K').
$$
No properness of $p_2$ or smoothness of $q_1$ is needed: this is the $!$-exchange clause. By [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the pullback-composition identifications in [lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower], rationalized,
$$Lr_{12}^*A\simeq Lr_1^*M\otimes^L_E Lr_{12}^*\mathcal K.$$
These isomorphisms are natural in all three objects.

Apply the compact-support projection formula of [prop-functor-package] to $f=r_{23}$, source object $Lr_{12}^*A$ and target object $\mathcal K'$. Its target finite-Tor condition holds because at field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Its isomorphism turns the last expression into
$$Rq_{2,!}Rr_{23,!}(Lr_{12}^*A\otimes^L_E Lr_{23}^*\mathcal K').$$
Use the composition clause of [prop-functor-package], $q_2r_{23}=r_3$, step 3, and the rationalized associator of [lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower]. The result is
$$Rr_{3,!}(Lr_1^*M\otimes^L_E Lr_{12}^*\mathcal K\otimes^L_E Lr_{23}^*\mathcal K').$$

Set $B=Lr_{12}^*\mathcal K\otimes^L_E Lr_{23}^*\mathcal K'$. The unshifted transform by the stated convolution is $Rs_{2,!}(Ls_1^*M\otimes^L_E Rr_{13,!}B)$. Use the tensor symmetry of [lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower], rationalized, to put $Rr_{13,!}B$ first. The projection formula of [prop-functor-package] for $r_{13}$, with source object $B$ and target object $Ls_1^*M$, gives
$$Rs_{2,!}Rr_{13,!}(B\otimes^L_E Lr_{13}^*Ls_1^*M).$$
Again its Tor hypothesis holds by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The pullback compositor identifies $Lr_{13}^*Ls_1^*M$ with $Lr_1^*M$. Tensor symmetry and associativity, followed by the compact-support compositor with $s_2r_{13}=r_3$, yield exactly the expression in step 4. All transformations used are natural. Compose the step-4 isomorphism with the inverse of this step-5 isomorphism to obtain the asserted natural isomorphism of unshifted functors; step 2 adds $[a+b]$. This compares the transforms and makes no uniqueness claim for their kernels.

For the Fourier assertion use the evaluation Artin--Schreier kernels of [def-fd-kernel] in the adic category stipulated by [def-fourier-set]: since $\mu_p\subset E$, the character values lift to $\mathcal O_E^\times$, and [def-fd-adic-fourier-realization] gives the completed realization $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{adic}}_{\Psi^{\pm1},b}\in D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ on the Noetherian products $V\times_SV^\vee$ and $V^\vee\times_SV''$ (characteristic $p$, finite type over $k$ by step 1); its rationalization is the kernel in $D^b_c(-,E)$. The two functors in the statement are precisely the just-treated kernel transforms with $a=b=r$ and with the dual bundle as the middle factor. Substituting these kernels in the convolution formula and $r+r=2r$ gives the claimed kernel and shift. This is only the composition formula; no computation of the convolution or inversion theorem is used. The normalization convention of [def-fd-transform] is exactly the displayed formula with shift equal to the rank $r$. This citation takes only that normalization: its discrete-module operations are not substituted for the adic operations explicitly specified here.

split_report.blueprint: First paragraph: steps 1--4 give the Cartesian square, shift bookkeeping, base change, pullback/tensor and first projection formula. Second paragraph: step 5 applies the second projection formula and compares the resulting functors. Step 6 specializes the kernels and shifts.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NZ-36e15d644 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item (six steps), the main-20261015 and master blueprint statement and proof, the unit, the statements of all 16 cited nodes and the two citers. There are no new nodes. The base is narrowed to S separated of finite type over k = F̄_q with E/Q_ℓ finite, which is the domain of prop-functor-package and def-fix-six-functor-datum, and the change is reported (E7). Both citers use S = Spec k. Replacing 'kernels agree' by a natural isomorphism of functors matches what the source actually proves and weakens nothing. Steps 1-5 check against the cited statements: the !-base change along q1 (clause 4, any base change); the projection formula for r23 and for r13 (clause 5, with ctf = c at E by def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude); composition and the pullback compositors; and the signed shift comparisons (lem-sf-completed-tensor-shift-right, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift). Small cases (point base, zero kernels, empty factor, a = -b, r = 0) all work. Fault C4/B3 is repaired: step 6 and the specialization took the adic E-kernels from def-fd-kernel, which defines only a discrete Λ-module sheaf. The FIX cites the existing def-fd-adic-fourier-realization (completed realization L^adic_{Ψ,b} in D^b_c(-,O_E) on Noetherian schemes of characteristic p, then rationalized) in the statement, stmt_deps, step 6 uses and proof_deps; it makes no cycle. The seven declared tool uses are accepted. No SGA source.
